shortlist.title: Can ChatGPT Decipher Fedspeak?
shortlist.authors: Anne Lundgaard Hansen; Sophia Kazinnik
shortlist.question: The hawk, the dove, and the disagreement
shortlist.concept: Commit to a policy-stance label, reveal human disagreement, then change negation/context and class prevalence in a confusion matrix.
shortlist.learn: Context and noisy labels matter; describing policy language is different from identifying an exogenous policy shock.
shortlist.caveat: Use curated original examples or rights-cleared excerpts; historical model labels stay historical and synthetic wording stays labeled.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: A supervised machine learning algorithm for detecting and predicting fraud in credit card transactions
shortlist.authors: Jonathan Kwaku Afriyie; Kassim Tawiah; Wilhemina Adoma Pels; Sandra Addai-Henne; Harriet Achiaa Dwamena; Emmanuel Odame Owiredu; Samuel Amening Ayeh; John Eshun
shortlist.question: The 96% detector and the overflowing review queue
shortlist.concept: Rebuild Table 7 as 96,961 transaction tiles; sort alerts, allocate reviewer capacity, then vary a labeled synthetic prevalence and loss ratio.
shortlist.learn: High accuracy and recall can coexist with about 9% precision when fraud is rare; costs determine whether the detector is useful.
shortlist.caveat: Table 7 implies recall about95.8%, differing from Table8's97%; show the recomputation, retain source values, and do not infer a threshold curve from one matrix.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Can ChatGPT forecast stock price movements? Return predictability and large language models
shortlist.authors: Alejandro Lopez-Lira; Yuehua Tang
shortlist.question: You understood the news. Did you arrive in time?
shortlist.concept: Commit to a direction, place an execution flag on a price timeline, then vary delay, cost and competing information processors.
shortlist.learn: A correct description of an initial price reaction is different from a tradable forecast of later drift.
shortlist.caveat: Preserve portfolio-day versus individual-stock definitions; synthetic latency paths cannot be presented as estimated historical returns.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Accuracy of Explanations of Machine Learning Models for Credit Decision
shortlist.authors: Andrés Alonso; José Manuel Carbó
shortlist.question: Can you audit an explanation?
shortlist.concept: Set a five-feature synthetic lending oracle, hide its settings, and compare the true feature ordering with a model explanation. Track predictive quality and explanation fidelity separately.
shortlist.learn: A model can predict well while misidentifying which features matter; predictive accuracy and explanation accuracy are separate properties.
shortlist.caveat: The paper benchmarks explanations on controlled synthetic credit-style data. Feature importance is not proof of causality in real lending. A correlated-proxy lab would be a separately labeled teaching extension.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: AI-Powered Trading, Algorithmic Collusion, and Price Efficiency
shortlist.authors: Winston Wei Dou; Itay Goldstein B; Yan Ji
shortlist.question: Two trading bots, no conversation
shortlist.concept: Move between quiet and noisy markets, inject a deviation, and force a new exploration step. Distinguish strategic punishment from similar mistaken beliefs behind apparently cooperative trading.
shortlist.learn: Similar high-profit outcomes can arise from different mechanisms; better individual learning does not automatically improve market information.
shortlist.caveat: This is a simulated possibility, not evidence of actual market misconduct. Use precomputed policies or a reduced teaching game; browser training is not a replication of the paper.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Financial Statement Analysis with Large Language Models
shortlist.authors: Alex G. Kim; Maximilian Muhn; Valeri V. Nikolaev
shortlist.question: The nameless company
shortlist.concept: Predict earnings direction from balanced synthetic statements; click ratios to reveal numerators and denominators, then unmask the name and compare benchmarks.
shortlist.learn: Arithmetic correctness, an earnings-direction forecast and an investment return are different targets.
shortlist.caveat: Pin the 2024 v1 source; no blanket GPT-beats-analysts claim, no assumption of universal immunity to leakage, and no redistribution of commercial fundamentals data.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Instruct-FinGPT: Financial Sentiment Analysis by Instruction Tuning of General-Purpose Large Language Models
shortlist.authors: Boyu Zhang; Hongyang Yang; Xiao-Yang Liu
shortlist.question: Good news relative to what?
shortlist.concept: Predict sentiment for a numerical release, reveal expectations, then adjust actual-versus-expected values and compare curated labels.
shortlist.learn: Financial sentiment depends on numerical context and the classification task, not just positive-sounding words.
shortlist.caveat: Examples and labels are task dependent; articleFigure1 contains surprising labels worth discussing, not silently correcting; a rule-based toy is not a tuned LLM.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: ChatGPT Informed Graph Neural Network for Stock Movement Prediction
shortlist.authors: Zihan Chen; Lei Zheng; Lu Cheng; Jialu Yuan; Di Zhu
shortlist.question: A news story draws an edge
shortlist.concept: Reveal a relation in a curated company news card; add/remove the inferred graph edge and trace one message-passing step into stock scores.
shortlist.learn: Relational structure can change a prediction even when each company's own features stay fixed.
shortlist.caveat: One propagation step is an interpretable teaching model, not a GNN backtest; inferred edges are not proof of causal supply-chain effects.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: A federated machine learning approach for order-level risk prediction in Supply Chain Financing
shortlist.authors: Lingxuan Kong; Zheng Ge; Alexandra Melike Brintrup
shortlist.question: The invoice knows something the company rating misses
shortlist.concept: Distribute synthetic invoice records across three firms; compare firm-level risk, local learning and federated updates under unequal sample sizes.
shortlist.learn: Order-level targets and firm-level labels differ; combining data can help a sparse firm while disturbing a richer local model.
shortlist.caveat: Federated learning alone is not a formal privacy guarantee; paper's aerospace case is not evidence of universal default prediction improvements.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Trading Automation in the Stock Market
shortlist.authors: Taylan Kabbani; Ekrem Duman
shortlist.question: Teach the trading agent the wrong reward
shortlist.concept: Choose profit, turnover and cost penalties in a small deterministic trading world; inspect the policy rather than a single winning path.
shortlist.learn: The reward, observability and market constraints shape what an RL agent learns.
shortlist.caveat: A reduced teaching game does not reproduce TD3 training or the reported Sharpe ratio; freeze random seeds and show out-of-sample regime changes.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Sentiment trading with large language models
shortlist.authors: Kemal Kirtac; Guido Germano
shortlist.question: The sentiment score meets the trading clock
shortlist.concept: Send the same curated headline scores through different execution delays and turnover budgets; compare signal accuracy with net outcomes.
shortlist.learn: A strong classification score does not guarantee robust implementable portfolio performance.
shortlist.caveat: Pin the LSE published copy; synthetic cost sweeps cannot validate the paper's backtest or eliminate possible temporal-contamination questions.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: FinRobot: An Open-Source AI Agent Platform for Financial Applications using Large Language Models
shortlist.authors: Hongyang Yang; Boyu Zhang; Neng Wang; Cheng Guo; Xiaoli Zhang; Likun Lin; Junlin Wang; Tianyu Zhou; Mao Guan; Runjia Zhang; Christina Dan Wang
shortlist.question: The financial agent's audit trail
shortlist.concept: Pass a question through data retrieval, calculation and report nodes; inject a stale number or missing citation and trace its propagation.
shortlist.learn: A multi-agent workflow is only as reliable as its evidence and checks; more agents do not guarantee truth.
shortlist.caveat: Use a deterministic staged simulator; it is not a functioning FinRobot deployment or a live financial adviser.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Forecasting Bitcoin Price Direction With Random Forests: How Important Are Interest Rates, Inflation, and Market Volatility?
shortlist.authors: Syed Abul Basher; Perry Sadorsky
shortlist.question: The feature-importance weather map
shortlist.concept: Move a rolling time window and forecast horizon; show how macro and technical importance rankings can change.
shortlist.learn: Feature importance is conditional on time, horizon, model and correlated alternatives.
shortlist.caveat: Use labeled synthetic windows unless the exact paper dataset is reproducible; feature importance is not macroeconomic causality.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Machine Learning Methods in Finance: Recent Applications and Prospects
shortlist.authors: Daniel Hoang; Kevin Wiegratz
shortlist.question: Predict, measure, or explain?
shortlist.concept: Put a finance question through three doors: predicting an outcome, creating a measure and extending an econometric tool; reveal different validation needs.
shortlist.learn: Prediction quality and causal explanation are not interchangeable research goals.
shortlist.caveat: Broad review makes an excellent methods orientation but should link to narrower mechanism papers rather than imitate their results.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: FinGPT: Open-Source Financial Large Language Models
shortlist.authors: Hongyang Yang; Xiao-Yang Liu; Christina Dan Wang
shortlist.question: The data freshness machine
shortlist.concept: Route a dated news packet through collection, cleaning, adaptation and evaluation; move a model's cutoff and count what becomes stale.
shortlist.learn: Fresh financial data, task accuracy and profitable information are different achievements.
shortlist.caveat: Use a tiny disclosed classifier and prerecorded outputs; the local model is not FinGPT or a replication of reported returns.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Is it all hype? ChatGPT’s performance and disruptive potential in the accounting and auditing industries
shortlist.authors: Marc Eulerich; Aida Sanatizadeh; Hamid Vakilzadeh; David A. Wood
shortlist.question: Did the model improve, or did its tools?
shortlist.concept: Give identical original accounting questions to a bare-response path and a calculator/tool path; toggle examples and error checks.
shortlist.learn: Model version, prompting, tools and question sampling all affect a benchmark comparison.
shortlist.caveat: Do not present published multiple-choice thresholds as proof of professional competence; use original questions, not licensed exam banks.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: ChatGPT: Unlocking the future of NLP in finance
shortlist.authors: Adam Zaremba; Ender Demir
shortlist.question: The paper written by the model
shortlist.concept: Pair a polished financial-AI paragraph with its cited evidence; identify what the text demonstrates and what it merely asserts.
shortlist.learn: Fluency can demonstrate text generation while leaving the financial claims untested.
shortlist.caveat: The foreword explicitly says ChatGPT wrote the paper; treat it as a meta-literacy exhibit, not evidence validating all its applications.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Artificial Intelligence in Auditing: A Conceptual Framework for Auditing Practices
shortlist.authors: Diogo Leocádio; João Reis; Luís Malheiro
shortlist.question: The auditor's evidence budget
shortlist.concept: Allocate limited review time across a miniature ledger; compare sampling, anomaly scores and independently verified exceptions.
shortlist.learn: Examining every transaction is different from establishing that each transaction is valid.
shortlist.caveat: The paper is a conceptual framework; the ledger and scoring model are educational extensions, not an empirical replication.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: Operational Research and Artificial Intelligence Methods in Banking
shortlist.authors: Michael Doumpos; Constantin Zopounidis; Dimitrios Gounopoulos; Emmanouil Platanakis; Wenke Zhang
shortlist.question: Which banking problem did you actually ask?
shortlist.concept: Choose credit allocation, efficiency or mergers; fit the question to prediction, optimization and causal evidence cards.
shortlist.learn: An accurate forecast does not itself specify a desirable banking decision.
shortlist.caveat: This is a survey map; all numerical mini-problems would be explicit educational examples grounded in cited methods.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.

shortlist.title: A scoping review of ChatGPT research in accounting and finance
shortlist.authors: Mengming Dong; Theophanis C. Stratopoulos; Victor Xiaoqi Wang
shortlist.question: The AI finance claim map
shortlist.concept: Sort research into AI as application, research instrument and institutional change; click through to a narrower falsifiable question.
shortlist.learn: A survey organizes questions; it does not establish that all proposed applications work.
shortlist.caveat: Retain survey dates and emerging-evidence limits; do not turn its catalog into a validated leaderboard.
shortlist.review: Selected source sections reviewed; not every appendix.
